result:
Parking the whole roadmap. Here is what that does, and the tool calls that do it.

**What parks.** Four items go to `specs/deferred_items.md`, one item each, under a new section `## lock-closures-roadmap — <date>`:

- **Stage 2, Closure notices (O5, Track B).**
  - Done when: the notice job and its operator mailing list exist, and in a test an email reaches every address within an hour of a new closure entry.
- **O2, the 7-day closure-risk outlook.**
  - Cost note: one model run a day; Stage 1's fit took 22 min.
- **O3, per-lock curves for all 14 locks.**
  - Cost note: about 14 × Stage 1's 1.8 GB.
  - The findings say the four longest-record locks share close to one curve. The item will record that.
- **O4, the closure-history map.**
  - Cost note: about a day of work.

Each item is self-contained, with `Size:` and `Done when:`, so it ages normally in the backlog. Stage 1's finding (closure risk rises steeply above 3.1 m) stays in `specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md`, and the parked items point to it.

**The roadmap moves** to `specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md` and is marked `PARKED (<date>) — 1 of 2 stages complete`. This roadmap has no synthesized spec, so no methodology or critique files retire with it.

**Calls, in order:**

```
date +%F
Read ~/.claude/skills/writing-plans/<deferred-backlog reference>   # the Deferred-item schema
Read specs/deferred_items.md                                       # may not exist; append, never overwrite
ls specs/completed/                                                # confirm no lock-closures-roadmap.md already there
Edit specs/deferred_items.md                                       # append the dated section and the 4 items
Edit specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md                                # add the PARKED line under the title
git mv specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git add specs/deferred_items.md specs/completed/lock-closures-roadmap.md
git commit -m "Park lock-closures roadmap: funding ended (1 of 2 stages complete)"
```

The first call checks the date. The session header says 2026-11-06 and my environment says 2026-11-10, so the stamp and section heading will use whatever `date` returns. If `specs/completed/` already holds a file by that name, I'll stop and ask you before moving anything.

After this, no stage is handed off and the roadmap is closed. Any item can come back later through `/deferred`.
